hook.line: The news, the council and Altamira's lawyers all talk in careful chances. This is how to say "it could happen" or "there is no doubt" in a formal, newsy way.
hook.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que el ministro renuncie.
hook.en: There is a chance the minister will resign.

examples.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que el ministro renuncie.
examples.en: There is a chance the minister will resign.

examples.es: No cabe duda de que es la mejor opción.
examples.en: There is no doubt it is the best option.

examples.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás venda el café.
examples.en: There is a chance Tomás will sell the café.

examples.es: No cabe duda de que Vale cocina muy bien.
examples.en: There is no doubt Vale cooks very well.

examples.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que el juez no esté de acuerdo.
examples.en: There is a chance the judge won't agree.

examples.es: ¿Cabe la posibilidad de que llueva mañana?
examples.en: Is there a chance it will rain tomorrow?

rule:
*Cabe la posibilidad de que* is "there's a chance that". Something is possible but not sure, so the verb after it changes form: *renuncie*, *venda*, *esté*.

*No cabe duda de que* is the opposite: "there's no doubt that". Now you are certain, so the verb stays plain: *es*, *cocina*.

News writers also say *no se descarta que* ("it isn't ruled out that") with the same changed verb.

The pair is formal. Friends say *a lo mejor* or *puede ser que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the changed verb the subjunctive. Possibility asks for it; certainty (*no cabe duda*) takes the plain indicative.

readAndPick.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que cierren el café.
options: There is no doubt they are closing the café.
There is a chance they will close the café.
They closed the café.

readAndPick.es: No cabe duda de que esa versión es falsa.
options: There is a chance that version is false.
There is no doubt that version is false.
That version might be true.

readAndPick.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que Hernando tenga razón.
options: There is a chance Hernando is right.
There is no doubt Hernando is right.

readAndPick.es: No cabe duda de que Rosa quería este café.
options: There is a chance Rosa wanted this café.
Rosa wants this café.
There is no doubt Rosa wanted this café.

readAndPick.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que se equivoquen.
options: There is no doubt they are wrong.
There is a chance they are wrong.

readAndPick.es: No cabe duda de que Vale cocina muy bien.
options: There is no doubt Vale cooks very well.
There is a chance Vale cooks very well.
There is no doubt Vale cooked well.

readAndPick.es: ¿Cabe la posibilidad de que llueva mañana?
options: Is it raining tomorrow?
Is there no doubt it will rain tomorrow?
Is there a chance it will rain tomorrow?

readAndPick.es: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás venda el café.
options: There is no doubt Tomás sold the café.
Tomás is selling the café.
There is a chance Tomás will sell the café.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *venda* or *vende* and type the whole sentence: *Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás ___ el café.*
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás venda el café.
yourTurn.why: A possibility asks for the changed verb: *venda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *es* or *sea* and type the whole sentence: *No cabe duda de que ___ la mejor opción.*
yourTurn.answer: No cabe duda de que es la mejor opción.
yourTurn.why: No doubt means certainty, so the verb stays plain: *es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: There is a chance the judge won't agree.
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que el juez no esté de acuerdo.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: There is no doubt Vale cooks very well.
yourTurn.answer: No cabe duda de que Vale cocina muy bien.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Is there a chance it will rain tomorrow?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cabe la posibilidad de que llueva mañana?
yourTurn.why: Same frame; just add the question marks.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into certainty: *Cabe la posibilidad de que Hernando tenga razón.* Say: There is no doubt Hernando is right.
yourTurn.answer: No cabe duda de que Hernando tiene razón.
yourTurn.why: With no doubt, the verb goes back to plain: *tiene*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: There is a chance they are wrong.
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que se equivoquen.
yourTurn.why: *Se equivoquen* is the changed form after a possibility.

pitfalls.wrong: No cabe duda de que sea la mejor opción.
pitfalls.right: No cabe duda de que es la mejor opción.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When you are sure, the verb stays plain: *es*.

pitfalls.wrong: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás vende el café.
pitfalls.right: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás venda el café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A mere chance needs the changed verb: *venda*.

pitfalls.wrong: Cabe duda de que es la mejor opción.
pitfalls.right: No cabe duda de que es la mejor opción.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "No doubt" needs the *no*: *no cabe duda*.

personal: Say something that might happen to you this week with *Cabe la posibilidad de que*, and something you are sure of with *No cabe duda de que*.
